subject: Trial deployment onboarding commitments / network & credentials
messages:
From: Michael Turner <m.turner@avatech.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Trial deployment — initial network details and timeline

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo last week — AvaTech is excited to start the trial. Per our conversation, we want to formalize a short mutual plan so our infra team can provision the VPC peering and IP allowlist while your team provisions the trial org and API keys.

High-level asks from our side:
- Can you confirm the sequence (org + api key creation vs peering) so we hand off to networking in the right order?
- What CIDR and peering IPs should our cloud team expect to see configured?
- Proposed start date: June 12; can we close by June 26 (two-week evaluation)?

I copied our platform engineer Sofia Ramos — she’ll be the day-to-day contact for peering and firewall changes.

Thanks,
Michael Turner
VP Product, AvaTech

--
AvaTech | m.turner@avatech.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Turner <m.turner@avatech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-04T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Trial deployment — initial network details and timeline

Hi Michael — great to hear and thank you.

Summary / proposed MAP:
- June 12: Redwood creates trial org, issues scoped API keys, and shares operational runbook (we’ll send keys to your security mailbox and a short checklist).
- June 13–14: AvaTech applies IP allowlist + initiates VPC peering request.
- June 15: Technical validation (smoke tests, simple inference call).
- June 18–25: Evaluation window (you run representative traffic).
- June 26: Close check-in & next-steps decision (purchase or extended eval).

Technical notes we need from Sofia (to set up peering + firewall rules):
- Public egress IP ranges (CIDRs) that will be allowed to call Redwood endpoints (if you are NATing, provide your egress CIDR).
- Whether you prefer VPC Peering or PrivateLink; we support both but peering requires route updates on your side.
- Contact for receiving the API key (security@avatech.com or a specific person).

I’ve attached a working MAP spreadsheet and a simple network diagram so your team can see what the peering handshake looks like (MAP_trial_timeline.xlsx, network-diagram.png).

Karthik — tagging you to confirm the peering handshake steps and whether we need any additional info (ASN, suggested BGP settings) for AvaTech. Grace — can you draft a short SOW addendum for the trial (I attached a draft).

Next steps: Michael — can Sofia share CIDRs and confirm the preferred key delivery channel by EOD Monday (June 5)?

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com | +1 (650) 555-0789

Attachments: MAP_trial_timeline.xlsx (spreadsheet), network-diagram.png (image), sow_draft_202806.pdf (PDF)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Turner <m.turner@avatech.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@avatech.com>
Date: 2028-06-05T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Trial deployment — initial network details and timeline

Hi team — quick technical checklist from my side to avoid back-and-forth:

1) API keys / org: we will create a trial org and a pair of API keys (admin & monitoring) on June 12. Keys are scoped to the trial org and expire at the end of the window unless you request renewal. We can also bind keys to source IPs.

2) IP allowlist: if you provide an egress CIDR we will whitelist it at the edge. Please confirm whether you have a single egress /24 or multiple ranges. If you prefer key-binding + allowlist, we recommend both for extra security.

3) VPC peering:
   - For AWS: we’ll provide our VPC ID and account. You’ll need to accept the peering request and add a route to the peered CIDR.
   - No BGP required for a simple peering. If you want cross-region routing or high-availability, call it out and we’ll propose PrivateLink.

4) Test plan: once peering and allowlist are configured we’ll run a short validation suite (3 sample requests: token auth, streaming, and long-prompt manage cache) and share logs.

I’ve included a minimal ASN/ID info blob in the attached SOW draft. Michael — if your infra team prefers a templated peering request we can send one.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com

From: Michael Turner <m.turner@avatech.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@avatech.com>
Date: 2028-06-06T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Trial deployment — initial network details and timeline

Soojin — thanks for the clear plan and Karthik for the checklist. Confirming our side:

- CIDRs: 198.51.100.0/24 (primary egress) and 203.0.113.0/28 (management VPN).
- Preferred: VPC peering (AWS), no BGP. Our infra will accept the peering request and add routes.
- Key delivery: security@avatech.com (we’ll rotate on our side once trial starts).

Sofia will create the peering request on June 13 and expect the Redwood peering invitation the same day. We agree to the suggested timeline starting June 12 and finishing the evaluation by June 26; we’ll use June 18 for the mid-trial sync.

I attached our internal network contact card and a sample peering request format (see network-diagram.png for topology).

Looking forward — please send the trial org invite and keys when ready.

Regards,
Michael Turner
VP Product, AvaTech
